svg.aria-label: Diagram: Amazon VPC Lattice now publishes Amazon CloudWatch metrics for VPC resources. Previously resource access logs were the primary way to see this traffic, but they required additional processing and provided limited real-time visibility. Resource owners get metrics for resource gateways and resource configurations, while consumers get metrics for resource endpoints, service network endpoints, and service network VPC associations. The owner metrics are BytesProcessed, PacketsDropped, NewFlows, ActiveFlows and PortAllocationErrors; the consumer metrics are BytesProcessed, PacketsDropped, NewFlows and ActiveFlows. The announcement suggests consumers can set CloudWatch alarms for when new flows drop to zero or dropped packets increase, catching an unreachable resource before their applications do. The documented reporting criteria complicate that: VPC Lattice reports these VPC resource metrics only for one-minute periods in which there is traffic. A resource that stops receiving traffic therefore publishes no datapoint at all rather than a zero, so a static threshold alarm looking for NewFlows at or below zero receives missing data instead of a breach and settles in INSUFFICIENT_DATA unless missing data is explicitly treated as breaching. The contrast is visible inside the same CloudWatch namespace, because the older target group and service metrics in AWS slash VpcLattice are documented as reported from the time the resource receives traffic, whether the value is zero or non-zero. Two reporting rules, one namespace. The second thing to know is who receives the data: these metrics are published only to the account that owns the resource gateway, and if the resource gateway is in a shared VPC subnet the participant account that owns the resource gateway receives these metrics, not the VPC owner, while service network owners do not receive these metrics at all. The team that operates the service network is therefore the one team with no view of this telemetry. Third, PortAllocationErrors counts connections the resource gateway could not establish because it could not allocate a source port, and increasing values usually mean the resource gateway needs more IPv4 addresses per ENI or more Availability Zones, neither of which can be changed on an existing resource gateway, so the remedy is to create a resource gateway with the settings you need and re-create your resource configurations on it. The warning metric and the migration arrive together. Dimension sets cannot be mixed: metrics are available only for specific dimension sets and you cannot combine dimensions from different sets, so you cannot filter by both Service Network Resource Association Id and Resource Gateway Id. Metrics are kept for 15 months, both parties can break metrics down by Availability Zone, and the capability is available in all AWS Regions where Amazon VPC Lattice is available.
svg.title: The metric that proves the resource is reachable stops publishing when it is not
svg.text: A zero-flow alarm on a metric that does not publish zeros.
“They can set CloudWatch alarms for when new flows drop to zero or dropped packets increase, catching an
unreachable resource before their applications do.”
The reporting criteria, from the metrics reference
“VPC Lattice reports this metric only for one-minute periods in which there is traffic.”
No traffic means no datapoint — not a datapoint of zero. A static threshold of NewFlows ≤ 0 is never
evaluated against a breach; it is evaluated against nothing.
Treat missing data as breaching, or the alarm sits in INSUFFICIENT_DATA through the whole outage.
Two reporting rules in one namespace
target groups, services “whether the value is zero or non-zero” → publishes zeros
VPC resources (new) “only for … periods in which there is traffic” → does not
Who gets the data, and who does not
“Service network owners don’t receive these metrics.”
Owner of the gateway gets owner metrics. Owner of the endpoint gets consumer metrics. In a shared VPC
subnet it is the participant that owns the gateway, not the VPC owner. The platform team sees nothing.
THE FIVE OWNER METRICS
BytesProcessed NewFlows
PacketsDropped ActiveFlows
PortAllocationErrors
Consumers get the first four, not the fifth.
THE ONE WITH NO IN-PLACE FIX
PortAllocationErrors means more IPv4 per ENI
or more AZs is needed. “You can’t change either
on an existing resource gateway”.
New gateway, re-create every configuration.
Dimension sets are fixed and cannot be mixed — no filtering by gateway and service-network association together.
Metrics are kept 15 months and can be split by Availability Zone, which is the one genuinely new diagnostic:
a single impaired AZ in a shared database path used to be invisible without processing access logs.
Available in all AWS Regions where Amazon VPC Lattice is available.
